The learner asks specifically: Make sure one of the senses is this meaning: for the reason that.

notes: In Greek, the same word is used for both the question 'why?' and the answer 'because'. For 'because', you can also use the slightly more formal 'επειδή'.

senses.definition: Used to ask for the reason or purpose of something.

examples.emotion: curious and waiting for an explanation

senses.definition: Used to introduce the reason for something.

examples.text: Δεν μπορώ να βγω γιατί έχω δουλειά.
examples.translation: I cannot go out because I have work.

notes: In Greek, the same word is used for both the question 'why?' and the answer 'because'. Context and the position of the word in the sentence usually make the meaning clear.
When used as 'because', it is often written as 'γιατί' without an accent (γιατι), though in modern standard Greek, the accented form is accepted for both meanings.

senses.definition: Used to ask for a reason or purpose.

examples.emotion: curious and waiting for an explanation

senses.definition: Used to introduce the reason for something; for the reason that.

examples.text: Δεν μπορώ να βγω γιατί έχω δουλειά.
examples.translation: I cannot go out because I have work.

faults.quote: When used as 'because', it is often written as 'γιατί' without an accent (γιατι)
faults.why: False: multisyllabic Greek words always take an accent; «γιατί» is always accented in both senses.
